questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT lists four processes that are basic to taxonomy. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

solution.explanation: Based on characteristics, all living organisms can be classified into different taxa; this process is taxonomy. External and internal structure, the structure of cells, the development process and the ecological information of organisms are essential and form the basis of modern taxonomic studies. Hence characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature are the processes that are basic to taxonomy. Hybridisation (crossing of organisms) is not one of them.
steps: Basic processes: characterisation, identification, classification, nomenclature
solution.why_others_wrong: Characterisation, identification and nomenclature are all named by NCERT, along with classification, as processes basic to taxonomy.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (taxonomy)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Hybridisation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The order Primata, comprising monkey, gorilla and gibbon, is placed along with the order Carnivora in the same:

solution.explanation: Class includes related orders. NCERT gives the example that the order Primata, comprising animals like monkey, gorilla and gibbon, is placed in class Mammalia along with the order Carnivora, which includes animals like tiger, cat and dog. Class Mammalia has other orders also.
solution.why_others_wrong: Hominidae is a family (of man), below the level of order. Diptera is the order of the housefly. Arthropoda is the phylum of the housefly, not of primates.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Taxonomic Categories (class)
solution.final_answer: Option A: class Mammalia

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Amoeboid protozoans live in fresh water, sea water or moist soil. Which of the following is cited by NCERT as an amoeboid protozoan that is a parasite?

solution.explanation: Amoeboid protozoans move and capture their prey by putting out pseudopodia (false feet), as in Amoeba. Marine forms have silica shells on their surface. Some of them, such as Entamoeba, are parasites.
solution.why_others_wrong: Paramoecium is a ciliated protozoan. Euglena is a euglenoid and Gonyaulax a dinoflagellate; neither is an amoeboid protozoan.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Protista (Protozoans)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Entamoeba

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In addition to proteins, viruses contain genetic material. NCERT states that viruses which infect animals have:

options.text: either single- or double-stranded RNA, or double-stranded DNA
both DNA and RNA in the same virus particle

solution.explanation: Viruses contain either RNA or DNA; no virus contains both. Viruses that infect plants generally have single-stranded RNA, and bacteriophages usually have double-stranded DNA. Viruses that infect animals have either single- or double-stranded RNA or double-stranded DNA.
steps: Animal viruses → ssRNA, dsRNA or dsDNA
solution.why_others_wrong: Only single-stranded RNA describes the viruses that generally infect plants. No virus contains both DNA and RNA. Animal viruses are not restricted to double-stranded DNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option B: either single- or double-stranded RNA, or double-stranded DNA

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT explains that 'insects' is a recognisable group that can be given a rank, because its members share common features such as:

options.text: a body covering of silica plates

solution.explanation: Insects represent a group of organisms sharing common features like three pairs of jointed legs. Such a group is a recognisable concrete object that can be classified, and it is therefore given a rank or category.
steps: Common feature of insects → three pairs of jointed legs
solution.why_others_wrong: A dorsal hollow neural system is a feature of chordates. Insects have three, not four, pairs of legs. Silica plates are not a feature of insects.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Taxonomic Categories
solution.final_answer: Option C: three pairs of jointed legs

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Nomenclature, or naming, is possible only when an organism is described correctly and we know to what organism the name is attached; this is identification.
Statement II: Systematics ignores evolutionary relationships between organisms and is based only on their external structure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that nomenclature or naming is only possible when the organism is described correctly and we know to what organism the name is attached to; this is identification. Systematics deals with the kinds of organisms and their diversities and also takes into account the evolutionary relationships between organisms.
steps: Statement II: false, systematics takes evolutionary relationships into account
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (identification, systematics)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (organism) with List-II (family).

List-I:
A. Homo sapiens (man)
B. Musca domestica (housefly)
C. Triticum aestivum (wheat)

List-II:

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In NCERT's table of organisms with their taxonomic categories, man belongs to the family Hominidae, the housefly to Muscidae and wheat to Poaceae. The genus Panthera, which includes the lion (Panthera leo), is placed with the genus Felis in the family Felidae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Bacteria are the most abundant micro-organisms, and hundreds of bacteria are present in a handful of soil.
Statement II: Mycoplasma includes many forms that are pathogenic in animals and plants.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that bacteria are the most abundant micro-organisms; they occur almost everywhere, and hundreds of bacteria are present in a handful of soil. Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall; they are the smallest living cells known, can survive without oxygen, and many are pathogenic in animals and plants.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A fungus had long been placed in Deuteromycetes because only its asexual stage was known. Later, it is found to produce ascospores in asci. Following the practice described in NCERT, this fungus would now be:

options.text: kept in Deuteromycetes, because its mycelium is septate

solution.explanation: Deuteromycetes are called imperfect fungi because only their asexual or vegetative phases are known. When the sexual (perfect) stages of these fungi are discovered, they are often moved to Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes. A fungus forming ascospores in asci has the sexual stage of an ascomycete, so it is moved to Ascomycetes.
steps: Perfect stage discovered → moved out of Deuteromycetes
solution.why_others_wrong: Once its perfect stage is known the fungus is no longer 'imperfect', so it is not kept in Deuteromycetes. Phycomycetes form zygospores and Basidiomycetes form basidiospores, not ascospores.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi (Deuteromycetes)
solution.final_answer: Option A: moved to Ascomycetes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Compared with many other organisms, bacteria as a group show the most extensive metabolic diversity.
Reason (R): The bacteria include photosynthetic autotrophs, chemosynthetic autotrophs and heterotrophs.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Though the bacterial structure is very simple, bacteria are very complex in behaviour; as a group they show the most extensive metabolic diversity. Some bacteria are autotrophic: they are photosynthetic (like cyanobacteria) or chemosynthetic (oxidising inorganic substances such as nitrates, nitrites and ammonia). The vast majority are heterotrophs. This range of modes of nutrition is what their metabolic diversity consists of, so R explains A.
steps: Photosynthetic, chemosynthetic and heterotrophic modes → metabolic diversity → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about protozoans are correct?

(a) All protozoans are heterotrophs and live as predators or parasites.
(b) Amoeboid protozoans live in fresh water, sea water or moist soil.
(c) Ciliated protozoans are actively moving organisms because of the presence of thousands of cilia.
(d) Sporozoans have an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle.
(e) All flagellated protozoans are free-living.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: All protozoans are heterotrophs and live as predators or parasites; they are believed to be primitive relatives of animals. Amoeboid protozoans live in fresh water, sea water or moist soil. Ciliated protozoans are aquatic, actively moving organisms because of the presence of thousands of cilia. Sporozoans include diverse organisms that have an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle. Flagellated protozoans are either free-living or parasitic, e.g., Trypanosoma, the parasite that causes sleeping sickness.
steps: (e): false, flagellates are free-living or parasitic
solution.why_others_wrong: Every wrong combination either leaves out a true statement or includes (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Protista (Protozoans)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a biological name is handwritten, the generic name and the specific epithet are underlined separately.
Reason (R): The separate underlining (or printing in italics) indicates the Latin origin of the two words.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics; they are Latinised or derived from Latin irrespective of their origin. Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined, or printed in italics, to indicate their Latin origin. So the purpose stated in R is the reason for the practice in A.
steps: Underlining/italics shows Latin origin → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (binomial nomenclature)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the twin characteristics of growth are:

options.text: increase in mass and accumulation of material on the surface
cell division and response to stimuli
increase in mass and increase in number of individuals

solution.concept: Growth as a feature of living organisms
solution.explanation: All living organisms grow. Increase in mass and increase in number of individuals are the twin characteristics of growth. A multicellular organism grows by cell division; in unicellular organisms growth by cell division also increases the number of individuals.
steps: Twin characteristics: increase in mass + increase in number of individuals
solution.why_others_wrong: Accumulation of material on the surface is how non-living objects such as sand mounds 'grow'. Response to stimuli and metabolism are separate features of living organisms, not the characteristics of growth.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (characteristics of living organisms)
solution.final_answer: Option C: increase in mass and increase in number of individuals

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about systems of classification are correct?

(a) The main criteria used by Whittaker include cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.
(b) The three-domain system divides kingdom Monera into two domains.
(c) In the three-domain system, the remaining eukaryotic kingdoms are placed in the third domain.
(d) The three-domain system reduces the number of kingdoms to three.
(e) Fungi were given a separate kingdom by Whittaker mainly because they are prokaryotic.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Whittaker's main criteria for classification include cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships. The three-domain system divides kingdom Monera into two domains, leaving the remaining eukaryotic kingdoms in the third domain, thereby giving a six kingdom classification. Fungi are eukaryotic; Monera is the only prokaryotic kingdom.
steps: (d): false, the three-domain system gives six kingdoms
solution.why_others_wrong: Any combination containing (d) or (e) is wrong, and one leaving out (c) is incomplete.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Introduction (five kingdom and three-domain systems)
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Methanogens are responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from the dung of ruminant animals.
Reason (R): Methanogens are photosynthetic archaebacteria that live mainly in hot springs.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Methanogens are archaebacteria present in marshy areas and in the gut of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes, and they are responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from the dung of these animals. Hot springs are the habitat of thermoacidophiles, and methanogens are not photosynthetic.
steps: R: false, methanogens live in marshes and the ruminant gut; thermoacidophiles live in hot springs
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera (Archaebacteria)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (taxonomic category) with List-II (description in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Genus
B. Family
C. Order
D. Phylum

List-II:
I. An assemblage of families that exhibit a few similar characters
II. Characterised on the basis of both vegetative and reproductive features of plant species
III. A group of related species with more characters in common than with species of other genera
IV. Classes comprising animals like fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera. Family has a group of related genera with still less number of similarities as compared to genus and species; families are characterised on the basis of both vegetative and reproductive features of plant species. Order is an assemblage of families which exhibit a few similar characters. Classes comprising animals like fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds along with mammals constitute the next higher category, phylum.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes interchange genus, family and order, whose descriptions differ in the rank of the units grouped.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Taxonomic Categories
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In Whittaker's table of the characteristics of the five kingdoms, the body organisation described as 'multicellular/loose tissue' belongs to kingdom:

solution.concept: Body organisation in the five kingdoms
solution.explanation: In the table of characteristics of the five kingdoms, the body organisation is cellular in Monera and Protista, multicellular/loose tissue in Fungi, tissue/organ in Plantae and tissue/organ/organ system in Animalia.
solution.why_others_wrong: Protista is cellular, Plantae tissue/organ and Animalia tissue/organ/organ system in the table.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Introduction (Table 2.1, characteristics of the five kingdoms)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Fungi

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Viruses are nucleoproteins, and their genetic material is infectious.
Statement II: The infectious agent discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971 was a protein that lacked any nucleic acid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that viruses are nucleoproteins and the genetic material is infectious. In 1971, T.O. Diener discovered a new infectious agent that was smaller than viruses and caused potato spindle tuber disease. It was found to be a free RNA, lacking the protein coat seen in viruses, and was named viroid. An infectious agent made of abnormally folded protein is a prion, not Diener's viroid.
steps: Statement II: false, Diener's viroid is a free RNA without a protein coat
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Fungi grow best in cold and dry places, which is why food is stored in a refrigerator.
Reason (R): Food is kept in a refrigerator to prevent it from going bad due to bacterial or fungal infections.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Fungi prefer to grow in warm and humid places. NCERT asks why we keep food in the refrigerator and answers that it is to prevent food from going bad due to bacterial or fungal infections; the cold slows their growth. A is false because fungi grow best in warm, humid conditions, not cold, dry ones.
steps: A: false, fungi prefer warm and humid places
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following descriptions of algae is given by NCERT?

options.text: Chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic organisms
Chlorophyll-bearing, vascular, autotrophic and largely terrestrial organisms
Simple, thalloid, heterotrophic organisms with a cell wall of chitin
Plants whose main body is a sporophyte differentiated into root, stem and leaves

solution.explanation: Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic (both fresh water and marine) organisms. They also occur in a variety of other habitats such as moist stones, soils and wood.
steps: Algae: chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic, largely aquatic
solution.why_others_wrong: Algae have no vascular tissue and are largely aquatic. A heterotrophic body with a chitin wall describes fungi. A sporophyte with root, stem and leaves describes pteridophytes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae
solution.final_answer: Option A: Chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic organisms

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In isogamous sexual reproduction, the fusing gametes are similar in size. In which alga are such gametes flagellated, according to NCERT?

solution.explanation: Fusion of two gametes similar in size is called isogamous. Such gametes can be flagellated and similar in size, as in Chlamydomonas, or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size, as in Spirogyra. Volvox and Fucus are oogamous.
solution.why_others_wrong: Spirogyra shows isogamy with non-flagellated gametes. Volvox and Fucus show oogamy, a large non-motile female gamete fusing with a smaller motile male gamete.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (sexual reproduction)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Chlamydomonas

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Compared with the algae, the plant body of bryophytes is described by NCERT as:

options.text: differentiated into true roots, stem and leaves with vascular tissue
a diploid sporophyte bearing sporangia on sporophylls
always unicellular or colonial and free-floating
more differentiated, thallus-like and prostrate or erect, attached to the substratum by rhizoids

solution.explanation: The plant body of bryophytes is more differentiated than that of algae. It is thallus-like and prostrate or erect, and attached to the substratum by unicellular or multicellular rhizoids. Bryophytes lack true roots, stem or leaves, though they may possess root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures.
solution.why_others_wrong: True roots, stem and leaves with vascular tissue and sporangia on sporophylls belong to the sporophyte of pteridophytes. A unicellular or colonial free-floating body describes some algae.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes
solution.final_answer: Option D: more differentiated, thallus-like and prostrate or erect, attached to the substratum by rhizoids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In mosses, the leafy stage of the gametophyte develops:

options.text: from the capsule of the sporophyte after meiosis
from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud
from gemmae formed in gemma cups

solution.explanation: The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte, which consists of two stages. The first stage is the protonema, which develops directly from a spore. The second stage is the leafy stage, which develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud and bears the sex organs.
steps: Secondary protonema → lateral bud → leafy stage
solution.why_others_wrong: The capsule produces spores, not leafy shoots. The zygote forms the sporophyte. Gemmae in gemma cups are the asexual buds of liverworts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes (mosses)
solution.final_answer: Option C: from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Gymnosperms include medium-sized trees or tall trees and shrubs.
Statement II: The roots of gymnosperms are generally adventitious roots.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The gymnosperms include medium-sized trees or tall trees and shrubs; the giant redwood tree Sequoia is one of the tallest tree species. The roots are generally tap roots. Roots in some genera have a fungal association (mycorrhiza), as in Pinus, while some, like those of Cycas, have small specialised coralloid roots.
steps: Statement II: false, gymnosperms generally have tap roots
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms

questions.question_text:

B. Stored food is mannitol or laminarin

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
